# Toast

A short message that confirms an action and goes away.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Content first</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:content-first;mode:light" title="Toast examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-toast--docs">Open Toast in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:content-first;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Content first:** Confirms a saved article.

- **Use it when:** Saved, sent, exported: something people should notice without stopping.
- **Not when:** A failure people must understand (alert or dialog), or a notice that stays (alert).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): Stays on the page.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): Needs an answer.

## How Content first uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">The words of an error</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Calm and helpful. Take the blame, offer the way forward.</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Blaming the reader</div></div><div class="cap">A calm error keeps the reader's trust. Example: “We could not save your email. Check it and try again.”</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A success message</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Warm and brief, with what happens next</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A bare &quot;Done&quot;</div></div><div class="cap">A warm close invites the reader back. Example: “You're in. The next issue arrives on Friday.”</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Toast looks the way it does because of 2 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Toast, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How does it sound?</b><code>voice.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Conversational</div><p>Talk to one reader, like a good editor.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: A calm note: You're all caught up.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>success</b>: Warm and brief, with what happens next.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: Calm and helpful: take the blame, offer the way forward.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Empty: icon</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">3</div><small>Toast decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many tones does it use?</b><code>voice.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">One per moment</div><p>Warm by default, calmer for errors.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: Calm and helpful: take the blame, offer the way forward.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code> <code>Badge: danger</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toast decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Write to one person: "you", not "users".
- Short sentences with room to breathe.
- Explain why before asking for anything.
- Use: Read, Save for later, You, Next issue. Avoid: Click here, Submit, Users, Content.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Browse guides

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is announced politely without taking focus, and stays long enough to read. undefined
- [ ] Nothing people must act on lives only in a toast. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toast
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Toast reads 3 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Toast's tokens to change Toast alone.
